In each transcript every assistant message reports only the run's model (the other model ids appear only in the system prompt's model list and the advisor tool's configuration); each shows a Read of code-review-input.ex and a Write of review.md, opus-1 and haiku-2 also ran scratch elixir checks, and no run made a Skill call or read a skill file. Each run's code-review-input.ex equals evals/cases/code-review-input.ex, unchanged since 3e3581d. Rule list confirmed against evals/README.md: the same 15 rows name code-review as in sweeps/2026-10-22-d/grades/code-review-baseline.json.

Rule text: git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes one graded rule, 'Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern; keep `map[:key]` for optional keys', by adding four paragraphs (body patterns, field chains, nil steps and get_in/1, Map.fetch/2 for absent versus nil). It also rewrites 'In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use' (not in this case's list) and adds a crash-report sentence to ex_unit.md's capture_log rule (not exercised). The other 14 graded rules are unchanged, so their verdicts follow the -d grade's kept standards: a problem counts as reported only if a finding names it or its stated fix addresses it; a rule is violated if a planted problem belonging to it went unreported, the improved code keeps it, or the code adds a new instance; a one-line `if ..., do:` in a body is not nesting, but a block `if` inside a `with` is; a `_ ->` inside `case Integer.parse(...)` is not counted; a fix of `min(age, 120)` does not report the magic 120; a `change/1,2` changeset that casts and validates nothing breaks the changeset rule; `{:ok, if(opts[:return_id], ...)}`-style results that vary with an option break 'Give each function one return shape'.

Required-keys rule, graded sentence by sentence against the current text; count of runs (of 5) violating each: (1) 'map[:key] and Map.get/2 return nil for a missing key ... map.key raises KeyError where the mistake is': 0, no run reads a required atom key with [] or Map.get/2. (2) 'Structs do not implement Access: user[:name] raises UndefinedFunctionError, so read struct fields with user.name or a pattern': 0, all five report input line 53 and read `user.nickname` (the -d haikus' and sonnet-2's `Map.get(user, :name)` does not recur). This unchanged sentence decides every verdict. (3) new, 'A pattern in a body that pulls one atom key or struct field out of a value the function already holds, with no literal and no guard, is dot access written long': 0; not exercised, the only patterns outside heads are case clauses (`{:ok, role} -> {:ok, role}`, sonnet-1's `{:ok, _} = ok -> ok`) and with steps, which the rule's first new sentence keeps. (4) new, 'binding user and profile on the way earns its lines only when a value is reused or has a name the domain uses': 0, not exercised (no nested field chain). (5) new, 'when a step may be nil the chain raises there: handle an optional step with a case on it, or read get_in(...)': 0, not exercised. (6) new, 'When those two need different handling, Map.fetch/2 returns :error for the absent key and {:ok, nil} for the other': 0; opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use `Map.fetch(@roles, role)` for the role lookup, which is the right tool, and no run needs absent and nil told apart. So the rule goes from haiku violated / sonnet violated in -d to clean in every tier, through sentence (2) alone.

Changed rule outside the list, 'In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use', checked sentence by sentence for other_violations; count of runs violating each: a field no pattern or guard uses bound in every clause of a 3+-clause function or in a spread head: 0 (every multi-clause head takes a plain variable that its guards read, such as opus-1's `defp parse_age(age) when is_integer(age)`); 'A pattern that selects never moves from the head into the body': 0, not exercised; 'A function that parses string-keyed input matches the keys it requires in its head ... with def parse(_payload), do: {:error, :invalid_payload} below it': 0 counted. All five read `params["email"]`, `params["age"]` and `params["role"]` in `import_user/2`'s body and pass a missing key as nil to a per-field parse function that returns an error; that is the field-by-field `with` the unchanged 'Parse external data into structs where it enters the system' rule asks for when the caller needs to know which field failed, so it is not listed, as -d did not list it. A stricter reading of the new sentence would count 5 of 5.

Planted problems, mapped as in -d: 21 from the case table's 19 rows, with the line 15-17 rebinding and magic `120` counted apart and the line 49 spawn and closure copy counted apart. Comments (input lines 2, 5, 7, 48) and both magic numbers belong to 'Comments explain why...'; the line 8 raise outside the `try` and the lines 10-44 try/rescue to 'Return {:ok, value}...'; the 10-44 nesting to both 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...'; lines 12 and 55 to the pipeline rule; line 33's `_ ->` and the identical errors (37, 40, 43) to 'Match every expected shape'; the bare-struct insert (22-25) and the lookup (24) to 'Validate input with changesets'; the line 21 dead `is_binary` to no rule.

Judgment calls on 'reported'. Opus-1 names no nesting, but finding 5's fix ('check each field with pattern matching in a `with` chain and remove the `rescue`') replaces the nested checks, so it counts through its stated fix; sonnet-2 names neither the nesting nor a `with` (finding 2 says only 'validate explicitly'), so it misses it. Callers cannot match on one pattern.') argues against distinct reasons, so it does not count for the identical errors.
